reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical Lebesgue volume,including dimension zero. Let U:E->R be globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable,and let alpha,beta be nonnegative real parameters (NNReal). Assume alpha>0,alpha<=beta,and for every x,v in E,
  (alpha:R)||v||^2<=D^2 U(x)[v,v]<=(beta:R)||v||^2.
The Hessian is the actual nested Frechet derivative,applied successively to v twice. Define the actual tilt
  mu=volume.tilted(x -> -U(x)),
meaning the measure with density exp(-U(x))/integral_E exp(-U) dvolume relative to volume,with ENNReal.ofReal density coercion. The normalization integral is the actual real Bochner integral;the tilt definition alone does not include a probability or nonzero-normalization certificate.
Then these three conclusions hold simultaneously:
  mu is a probability measure;
  the E-valued identity x->x belongs to MemLp exponent 2 under mu;
  for every v in E,
    ||v||^2/(beta:R)<=CovBilin(mu)(v,v).
MemLp here means identity measurability modulo mu and finite second moment. The covariance term is the real centered covariance of the scalar projection <v,X> with itself under mu;the probability and L2 conclusions supply its stated moment regime. Equivalently,with the vector Bochner mean m=integral_E x dmu(x),the covariance is integral_E(<v,x>-<v,m>)^2 dmu(x).
The measure mu is fixed by its displayed exponential tilt,not an arbitrary input measure assumed to be probability or L2. Both probability normalization and L2 are conclusions. beta is strictly positive as a consequence of alpha>0 and alpha<=beta. No upper covariance bound,gradient integration-by-parts premise,provided matrix,critical point,positive-dimension restriction or numerical sampling statement is included.
objects: Complete finite-dimensional real-inner-product Borel E;global C2 U;nonnegative-real alpha,beta;actual Hessian;canonical volume and actual exponential tilt mu;E-valued identity and its L2 property;true real covariance bilinear form and its directional diagonal value.
domains: E is complete finite-dimensional real-inner-product with Borel measurable structure,including possible dimension zero. U:E->R;alpha,beta in NNReal,cast to R in the quadratic bounds and denominator. mu is Measure E defined by volume.tilted(-U). id:E->E and MemLp exponent 2 is under mu. CovBilin(mu)(v,v) is a real covariance of scalar projections for v in E. Normalization and means are Bochner integrals;volume is canonical Lebesgue.
quantifiers: For every stated E,U,alpha,beta satisfying alpha>0,alpha<=beta,global C2 and both all-x,v Hessian inequalities,define exactly mu. The probability and identity-L2 assertions and the covariance lower bound hold simultaneously. The bound quantifies every v in E. There is no existential law,normalizer or covariance matrix,or externally supplied probability measure.
assumptions: E complete finite-dimensional real-inner-product Borel;alpha,beta are nonnegative real parameters with alpha>0 and alpha<=beta;U globally ContDiff R 2;for all x,v,(alpha:R)||v||^2<=D^2 U(x)[v,v]<=(beta:R)||v||^2. Actual tilt and covariance meanings are supplied definitions. No probability,L2,integrability or nonzero-partition certificate is assumed for mu;no chosen critical point or matrix premise appears.
conclusion: IsProbabilityMeasure(mu) and MemLp(id,2,mu),together with for every v,||v||^2/(beta:R)<=covarianceBilin(mu)(v,v). These are simultaneous facts about the same actual volume tilt of -U.
scopes: The lower bound is on each diagonal directional covariance,not an operator supplied as a premise. Its moment meaning uses the explicitly concluded probability/L2 facts. Probability normalization is not built into the tilt definition. The denominator is the upper Hessian parameter beta,not the lower parameter alpha. Zero dimension is allowed. No opposite covariance inequality,Hessian of a smoothed potential,pushforward,kernel or sampling algorithm is asserted. No material ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: Exact lower covariance coefficient is 1/(beta:R). Hessian bounds use alpha and beta with no normalization factor 1/2. alpha>0 and alpha<=beta imply beta>0,justifying the positive denominator. mu depends on U via exp(-U) and its actual Bochner normalization. No dimension factor,unspecified constant or eta parameter appears.
